headline: Twin Peaks Campground and Border Access
reservation: Reservations for Twin Peaks Campground are highly recommended via Recreation.gov, especially during the peak winter months. Backcountry camping requires a separate permit obtained at the Kris Eggle Visitor Center. Systems are subject to change; always verify current monument status on the official NPS site.

days.title: Cactus Forest Loops

stops.name: Kris Eggle Visitor Center
stops.detail: Gather essential desert safety information and view interpretive exhibits on Sonoran biodiversity.

stops.name: Ajo Mountain Drive
stops.detail: Traverse the 21-mile gravel loop to see dense stands of organ pipe and saguaro cacti.

days.driving: Allow 3 hours for the scenic loop; conditions vary on unpaved surfaces.
days.note: High-clearance vehicles are not required for Ajo Mountain Drive, but avoid the route after heavy rain.

days.title: High Desert Views

stops.name: Bull Pasture Trail
stops.detail: Ascend into the Ajo Mountains for panoramic views of the monument and Mexico.

stops.name: Arch Canyon
stops.detail: View a natural rock arch high in the canyon walls along this shorter trail.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for transit to trailheads; conditions vary by heat.
days.note: Start all hikes before 9 AM to avoid peak midday desert temperatures.

days.title: Historic Oases

stops.name: Quitobaquito Springs
stops.detail: Visit this rare desert spring and pond that supports unique pupfish and lush vegetation.

stops.name: Victoria Mine Trail
stops.detail: Walk to the remains of a historic silver and gold mining operation from the 1800s.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for travel to Quitobaquito; conditions vary near the border.
days.note: Quitobaquito is near the international border; follow all posted signage and stay on trails.

intel.title: Trailhead Capacity
intel.text: Parking at Bull Pasture and Victoria Mine is limited to small lots. Arrive early during the winter peak to ensure a space.

intel.title: Remote Communication
intel.text: Cellular service is virtually non-existent once you leave the Highway 85 corridor. Inform others of your route before departing the visitor center.

intel.title: Gateway Supplies
intel.text: There is no fuel available inside the monument. Fill your tank in Ajo or Why before entering the park boundaries.

intel.title: Winter Peak
intel.text: January and February are the busiest months. Expect campground stays to be fully booked well in advance during this window.

intel.title: Border Checkpoints
intel.text: Internal roads are subject to Border Patrol presence. Travelers should carry identification and expect routine checkpoints on Highway 85.

plan.arrival: Fly into TUS, rent a vehicle, and purchase all water and food supplies in Tucson or Ajo before the 3-hour drive to the monument.
plan.vehicle: A standard car works for most main roads; check rental terms for driving on unpaved surfaces like Ajo Mountain Drive.
plan.goldenHour: The Desert View Trail offers a silhouette of saguaros against the sunset; timing varies by winter month.
